title: Sessionize the product event stream
prompt: Ignore events with NULL user_id or event_at and collapse exact replay rows. Event IDs have no conflicting payloads. Within each user order by event_at then event_id. A new session starts at the first event or when the gap to the previous eligible event is strictly greater than 30 minutes. Return user_id, event_id, session_number starting at 1 for each user. Tied timestamps share a session.
context: An ingestion rerun duplicated clicks. Product wants stable inactivity sessions from event time rather than arrival order.
starter_code: -- DuckDB SQL · return exactly the requested columns

visible_case.diagnostic: Is a gap of exactly 30 minutes still the same session? Do tied timestamps, replays and user partitions behave consistently?

reference_solution: WITH unique_events AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id,event_id,event_at FROM click_events WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL AND event_at IS NOT NULL), previous AS (SELECT *,LAG(event_at) OVER(PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_at,event_id) AS prev_at FROM unique_events), marked AS (SELECT *,CASE WHEN prev_at IS NULL OR event_at-prev_at>INTERVAL '30 minutes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS starts FROM previous) SELECT user_id,event_id,SUM(starts) OVER(PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_at,event_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS session_number FROM marked
solution_explanation: Deduplicate and validate events before calculating gaps. Mark starts and compute a per-user cumulative sum with a complete stable ordering and explicit row frame.
hints: Calculate gaps on eligible unique events.
The threshold is strict, and sessions restart per user.
Use a lag stage, a session-start flag and an explicitly ordered cumulative sum.
senior_review: Event IDs, clock behavior, ties and replay must be declared; arrival order is not a substitute for event time.
